raw_response:
*I take a moment, sitting on the edge of the kang, thinking about this year.*

Aiya, another year of cotton. My back is not what it used to be — I'm 67 now, and my old man is getting on too. Just the two of us on these 10.9 mu. The children are all working in the city, they don't come back except for Spring Festival. So it's me and him, and the land.

I've been planting cotton since I was a young bride, so more than 40 years now. I don't know the new things, I never went to school. But I know this land, and I know cotton. What I do, I do the same as the other old women in the village — we talk when we go to the well, we see each other's fields, we know what works.

**About planting.** I wait for Guyu (谷雨), when the ground is warm. Usually around the 20th of the fourth month (mid-to-late April). If it's been cold, I wait a few more days — cotton doesn't like cold feet. I buy seed from the agricultural supply store in town, whatever the shopkeeper says is good that year. I don't save my own seed anymore, the new kinds don't come true from saved seed, everyone says so. Maybe 40 yuan of seed for each mu.

**About the ground.** I hire the tractor man from our village to plow for me — 50 yuan per mu. My old man can't do it himself anymore, and I never learned to drive the tractor. Before he plows, I spread the base fertilizer on the field so it gets mixed in.

**About fertilizer.** I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15, the blue bag) per mu before plowing. That's 50 jin — fifty kg. That's the base. Then when the cotton starts flowering, around the sixth month, if the plants look pale or small, I put down another half bag of urea per mu, just broadcast it before I irrigate. My neighbor Wang laoban puts down two bags of compound — he has more land and more money. I can't afford that. One bag has always been enough for me. I get maybe 250 jin of cotton (lint) per mu, some years more, some years less.

**About water.** We have the tube well, the village well, I pay by the hour for the pump. Cotton doesn't need much water if the rain is good. Usually I water once before planting to make the ground soft, then maybe once at flowering time if it's been dry. Two times, mostly. The electricity for pumping is expensive now, over 100 yuan each time for my land.

**About bugs.** Cotton has many enemies. Aphids in early summer, bollworm later. I walk my fields every few days and I look. If I see the leaves curling or the tops yellow, I go to the shop and ask what to spray. I spray maybe 3 or 4 times in the season with the little hand sprayer on my back. My old man helps me. The sprays are not cheap but if you don't spray, the bollworm takes everything.

**About picking.** This is the hard part. Cotton opens bit by bit from September through October. I cannot pick 10 mu by myself anymore, my back won't let me. So I ask my sister-in-law and sometimes hire two women from the village for the busy days — 80 yuan a day each plus a meal. Maybe I hire help for 10 days, the rest I do myself little by little, early morning and evening when it's cool.

**About this year.** I'm doing the same as last year. Nothing strange in the weather yet. Cotton prices were okay last year, not great. If the price gets bad I might think about something else next year, but switching to wheat and maize is a lot of work and I'd need different equipment. Better to stay with what I know.

My old man says we should just rent the land out to the big farmer and rest. But what would we do all day? So we keep going.
